note: 205: design_check.py's thresholds and source classes. Every number is a candidate, to be tuned from data (Matt, 2026-11-12). The principles they encode are in docs/principles.md, *Design warnings*.

scarce_resources.note: tier-2 and capstone resources: scarce and earned; no cheap standard-action source

share_exempt.note: 226: a resource and source/spend that may exceed the share cap, listed as information with why
share_exempt.ambassadors standard:liberate: Liberate is the win route (Matt, 2026-11-13): ambassadors exist to free cities, so most of them going there is the design, not one spend crowding the rest

source_classes.note: regexes on games.jsonl's source keys (own:/other: stripped). 'standard' is a standard action or the antimatter action; tier-1 sources are found from content (own:play:/own:use: of a tier-1 card).

repeat_powers.note: a power name, or a power's effects (cost aside), on this many boards or more

standard_actions.note: each standard action's give and get at the unit anchors (docs/card-guidelines.md, *Unit anchors*; values.json for units with none). A number is a count; a string is a baseline.json param (module.param). 'src' is its games.jsonl source key, for its uses a game. 'off' (208, P1): the tunable that turns the action off at 0; such a row is skipped. 'narrative' (204): the story tag of its Sway. 'priced_in' (226): get units another unit's anchor already holds, not counted twice. 'exempt' (226): why the row may sit over the cap, listed as information.

rows.name: Liberate a city
rows.exempt: the win route (Matt, 2026-11-13): never a poorly priced hedge; its 5 Sway are in the city's 45 (priced_in)

extra_anchors.note: units the anchor table and values.json lack, from card-guidelines.md's derived lines and past checks (206: a node at values.json's 8; a factory at +1 chip income, 19; 210: a land token lifted at 3 rounds of a face-up token's 1 Discord, a sway 4 each, 12)

tag_story.note: 212: what each tag means in the story, as the ops it owns. An op key is `op`, or `op:resource` / `op:kind` / `op:side` where the op names one (opkeys.py in 212's results lists them). A card or tag-paid power whose effects hold an owned op, none of them owned by one of its tags, is a mismatch (`tag-story`). Ops in no tag's list (draws, credits, triggers, counters) are neutral: any tag may print them. `exceptions`: item -> why its story overrides the table, listed as information.

security.story: force and protection: troops, agents, hardening, shelters, defending nodes

diplomacy.story: cooperation: ambassadors, trust, Unity, working with humans, green energy and cleanup

science.story: discovery: insight, research cubes, stations, megaprojects, forecasting, particle physics

power.story: energy and antimatter: generation, grids, fusion, the weapons antimatter feeds

cyber.story: the network: botnets, Exploits, nodes, compute, firewalls, corruption, information

tag_story.neutral_why: neutral by design (any tag prints them): draws, credits, triggers and thresholds; threat counters (jam, auto_counter), since every tag answers threats its own way; liberate, the capstone every tag route reaches (player-cards.md, *The liberate capstones*); a tag's own payoffs (gain_per_tag, production_per_tag, income_per_tag, card_discount), which pay for the tag they count; reuse and choose_player, which only point another effect

exceptions.ais:researcher:Disrupt: a Cyber card hacks troops (drones) anywhere in a country, no reach: the Researcher's troop answer is remote by design (206), so it is paid in Cyber, not Security

sway.note: a narrative tag (204) on a sway source: its expected side. Until tags exist, sources are listed as information.

usage.note: 207: each player action's expected use, a band by role (candidates for Matt). Pooled over levels and boards, over the seat-games that could take it (a power: its board's seats). Measures: seat_round (uses a seat-round; a once-a-round action's share of rounds), seat_game (uses a seat-game), games (share of seat-games with a use), spent (a resource's spent over gained). A row's band overrides its role's; 'off' (a baseline param, or true) lists it as off. `design_check.py READ --usage` prints the inventory.

node-power.why: the board's node route, once a round: most rounds, never every round (a node is always right then)

board-engine.why: the board's signature 'each round you may' power: most rounds, not all

sacrifice.why: a tag-sacrifice power for cards you are done with: a use every game or two, never a round staple

troop-response.why: answers troops when they come: used in most games that have them, not a round staple

hedge.why: a luck hedge or desperate source, poorly priced by design: rare but not zero. 228: 0.5 -> 0.75: at r99 Make antimatter, Remove a troop and Sell a card, priced 0.2-0.6 at the anchors, sat at 0.53-0.57 a seat-game, a use every second game: rare, not a route

burn.why: 219 (Matt): a board's antimatter burn of its own engine: used but rare, the plants being the steady source

win-route.why: a Unity route the win runs through: most games, not every game (another route must exist)

sway-tool.why: a secondary Unity or Discord lever: used, never the route

staple.why: a standard economy action: used in some rounds, never crowding the round

cards.why: cards are the game: plays most of a round's actions

building.why: a building's once-a-round Action: the engine running

converter.why: a completed megaproject's once-a-round converter: used once it opens, not every round from the start

threat.why: paying a threat's counter: threats are answered, not ignored, and not the whole game

correction.why: taking back a commitment: zero is fine, often means misplays

resource.why: a resource gained is spent (engines over dials); over 1.1 is a start stock spent down

off.why: off at this revision's tunables or granted by no card: listed, no band

rows.why: Builder: credits into chips, its resource. 228: a credit converter, taken when credits are spare after cards: it pays 2.0x at the anchors, the agents' table at the chip anchor (6, not 4) left it at 0.28 a seat-round (+0.1 a game), so the band, not the price or the table, was the error
Builder: a chip into 2 cards, its draw
Protector: energy into hardening, its defense
Researcher: 2 insight into a card, its draw

Researcher: credits into a cube on a megaproject, its cubes. 228: a credit converter like Mint (2.0x at the anchors); +1 insight on it moved it only 1.73 -> 1.84 a game and no pair, so the band was the error

228 (Matt, amendment 10157: overuse alone is no reason to nerf; widen the band unless the Protector's pairs lead by over 5 after the weaker boards' buffs): 2.40 a seat-game at r99 and r100 on 46912-46975, the Protector's board 1.7-2.8 over the pair mean at d1-d2
219: the Researcher's antimatter, a research station of its own burned
219: the Builder's antimatter, a factory of its own burned (Fallout left)
219: the Protector's antimatter (227: Seize renamed Reclaim), a corrupted station or factory turned neutral (priced well above Remove a troop)
228: Patrol pushes agents as well as troops; with Remove agents at 2 ambassadors (r100) it is the Protector's cheap agent answer: 2.19-2.36 a seat-game at r99, 2.42-2.74 at r100 (46912-46975)

rows.name: Remove agents
rows.why: 228 (Matt, 2026-11-13: standard actions are poorly priced hedges, never the better route): 2 ambassadors for 3 agents (0.94) from r100; 1.4-1.6 a seat-game at 1 ambassador, 0.4 at 2

rows.name: Lift Fallout
rows.why: 210 (Matt, candidate): the one standard action that removes corruption, costly but not absurd; a rare hedge. 228: the cap back to the hedge's 0.5 (was 0.2 while Fallout was under 1 token a game, message 9540): 227 made Fallout a common harm on purpose (0.5-1 lift a game targeted)

rows.name: Envoy
rows.why: 228: a standard action is a poorly priced hedge, never the better route (Matt): an ambassador (8) for 1 Discord off (4), when the same ambassador is a fifth of a Liberate (the win route), so zero use is the design, not a fault

rows.name: Counter a threat whole
rows.why: the counter that asks more than resources

victory_needs.note: engines over dials: at high difficulty a win needs chips, energy, antimatter and cubes; warns when one is spent in under this share of won games

tokens.note: table work a round: the adversary's ops (games.jsonl adversary_ops) and these player-side counters, per round, against --old

dials.note: a baseline.json number moved by this share or more in a change that also edits content/ or a module's rules
